quantitative-aptitude-and-logical-reason.title: profit and loss relations with CP = 200
rows: SP - CP when SP exceeds CP
(SP - CP) / CP x 100, always on CP
discount / MP x 100, always on MP
quantitative-aptitude-and-logical-reason.note: Profit and discount sit on different bases: profit on cost price, discount on marked price, so a discount can still leave a profit.

quantitative-aptitude-and-logical-reason.title: why the alligation ratio is (d - m) : (m - c)
symbols: price per unit of the cheaper ingredient
price per unit of the dearer ingredient
price per unit of the mixture
quantity taken from the cheaper ingredient
quantity taken from the dearer ingredient
quantitative-aptitude-and-logical-reason.note: The mixture must cost exactly what its parts cost, so how far each price sits from the mean fixes the ratio of quantities.

quantitative-aptitude-and-logical-reason.title: parts of an argument and how each is tested
rows: accept it as given, even if it is false
must follow, not merely be plausible
negate it: if the conclusion collapses, it is an assumption
the step from premises to conclusion
watch for a term that appears only in the conclusion
a sentence that is true or false
quantitative-aptitude-and-logical-reason.note: The assumption is the part never written down, so the negation test is the only reliable way to expose it.

quantitative-aptitude-and-logical-reason.title: counting facts that decide a cube question
rows: each face shares an edge with 4 others
each corner touches 3 mutually adjacent faces
all except the face itself and its opposite
opposite pairs on a standard die
quantitative-aptitude-and-logical-reason.note: A face is adjacent to four of the other five, so one view can never identify its opposite; a second view is always needed.
